full_judgment:
2. Relevant facts necessary for disposal of the aforesaid petitions are that the writ petitioner Md Wais Hossain being aggrieved by the order of the Revenue Officer in Objection Case No 1634 filed an appeal under rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 being Appeal No. 108449 of 2007, the appeal was heard by Zonal Settlement Officer, Jessore Zone, Jessore and the Appeal Officer (hereinafter referred to as the Zonal Settlement Officer) and the Zonal Settlement Officer upon hearing both the parties by order No. 4 dated 19-12-2007 allowed the said appeal; after passing the aforesaid order in Appeal No. 108449 of 2007, Jahanara Khatun and others filed Miscellaneous Case No. 139 of 2013; thereafter, the Sadar Assistant Settlement Officer, Jessore Zone, Jessore (shortly, Sadar Assistant Settlement Officer) issued a notice vide Memo No. জোসেঅ/যশো/৬/৩২/খন্ড-৬/এস-১১১০ dated 31-3-2013 (the impugned notice) to the writ petitioner for appearing before the Zonal Settlement Officer i.e. the Appeal Officer; earlier a three members committee was formed for giving opinion in respect of re-hearing of the appeal and the said committee upon thorough examination and consideration of the materials on record, on 18-11-2012 opined that there was/is no scope of re-hearing of the appeal but it was not considered by the Zonal Settlement Officer. Whereupon, the writ petitioner respondent preferred Writ Petition No. 3697 of 2013 and obtained a Rule. 

 6. Subsequently, on an application of Jahan Ara Khatun a three members committee was constituted to examine the matter and the committee gave opinion dated 18-11-2012 stating that there is no scope of re-considering of the aforesaid appeals. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid opinion of three members committee dated 18-11-2012, Jahan Ara Khatun filed another applications to reconsider the appeals as per section 42A of the Rules alleging fraud. Whereupon, the Zonal Settlement Officer, Jessore Zone, in order to ensure justice entertained the aforesaid applications and appointed the Sadar Assistant Settlement Officer, to inquire into the matter and report thereon vide Memo No. 76 dated 13-1-2013. Accordingly, the Sadar Assistant Settlement Officer, Jessore Zone (respondent No. 4) upon a thorough inquiry and on careful scrutiny of the appeal proceedings detected that the verdict dated 19-12-2007 in Appeal No. 108449 of 2007 was passed on the basis of a so-called Sale Deed No. 7873 dated 11-12-2009, which appears to be an impossibility. The writ petitioner annexed a typed copy of the order dated 19-12-2007 to the writ petition wherein a reference of a Deed being Deed No. 7875 dated 11-12-2007 was given. Writ respondent No. 7 collected the last Sale Deed executed and registered in the year 2007 which was Deed No. 5851 dated 31-12-2007 and it clearly shows that the petitioner exercised fraud in obtaining the order dated 19-12-2007; after going through inquiry and considering the relevant documents, the Sadar Assistant Settlement Officer, found out about the aforesaid fraudulent act of the petitioner and so, he gave an opinion to the effect that the appeal judgment dated 19-12-2007 was a deceptive judgment and apt to be heard again oil that ground. Following the report dated 21-3-2017 issued by the Sadar Assistant Settlement Officer, Jessore Zone, the Zonal Settlement Officer, Jessore Zone, directed the Sadar Assistant Settlement Officer, to issue notices to the concerned parties to appear before him with connected papers in order to verify the facts and truth. Thereafter, the respondent No. 4 issued the impugned Notice vide Memo No. জোসেঅ/যশো/৬/৩২/খন্ড-৬/এস-১১১০ dated 31-3-2013 for re-hearing of the said appeal. After passing of the order in Appeal No. 108449 of 2007 the said Jahan Ara Khatun and others did not file the Miscellaneous Case No. 139 of 2013 against the judgment and order of Appeal Nos. 109316 of 2008, 109317 of 2008, 108449 of 2007, 140202 of 2010 rather Jahanara Khatun and others filed applications under section 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 before the Zonal Settlement Officer demanding rehearing of Appeal Nos. 109316 of 2008, 109317 of 2008, 108449 of 2007 and 140202 of 2010 upon setting aside the appeal orders passed earlier by him as the said was obtained by practicing fraud. The said application has been treated by the concerned office as Miscellaneous Case No. 139 of 2013' in order to examine and scrutinize the merit of the claim. The writ respondents prayed for dismissal of the Rule. 

 10. He further submits that the Appeal-Officer, then conducted another inquiry through a single person and he gave a report dated 24-3-2013 stating that the appeal Judgment dated 19-12-2007 was a deceptive Judgment and so, the matter is apt to be heard again on that ground. He also submits that subsequent enquiry was done by a person, who was one of a member of the committee, who gave the earlier opinion dated 18-11-2012. He next submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that correction of entry had been procured by practicing fraud and, as such, the Appeal Officer was empowered under Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 (hereinafter stated as the Rules) to review/rehear the appeal under Rule 31 of the said Rules and, as such, the Miscellaneous Case was legally entertained by the Zonal Settlement Officer and notice was also lawfully issued by concerned officer at his instruction. He finally submits that High Court Division failed to consider the fraudulent act of the writ petitioner for which the Miscellaneous Case was lawfully entertained and notices were issued to the concerned parties to appear before him with connected papers in order to verify the facts and truth and on the basis of the said order respondent No. 4 legally issued the impugned notice and, as such, the impugned Judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. 

 12. Mr Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Senior Advocate instructed by Mr, Md, Zahirul Islam, the learned Advocate-on-record appearing for the respondents in both the cases supports the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and submits that there is no element of fraud and, as such, there is no scope for review/re-hearing of the rule 42A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Rules, 1955. 

 15. We have also examined the relevant provision of Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 which reads as under: "42A. Correction of fraudulent entry before final publication of record-of-rights —The Revenue-officer, with the additional designation of 'Settlement Officer' shall, on receipt of an application or on receipt of an official report for the correction of an entry that has been procured by fraud in record-of-rights before final publication thereof, after consulting relevant records and making such other enquiries as he deems necessary, direct excision of the fraudulent entry and his act in doing so shall not be open to appeal. At the same time, the Revenue-officer shall make the correct entry after giving the parties concerned a hearing and recording his finding in a formal proceeding for the purpose of future reference." 

 18. Similarly in Aftab Ali Sheikh vs Director, Land Records, reported in 58 DLR 397 wherein it has been held that: "Under Rule 44 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955, the Director of Land Records and Surveys has been vested with the power to discharge all the functions of a Revenue Officer under the said chapter and shall have all the powers of a Settlement Officer under Rule 42A along with some other Rules in respect of all operations under Chapter XVII of the SAT Act but unless there is a case of fraud or having procured the appellate judgment in making the entry by fraud Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 has no manner of application." 

 19. In this decision also it has been clearly stated that in case of making entry by practicing fraud Rule 44A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 has no manner of application. In the instant case respondent No. 7 as well as the Government clearly stated that fraud has committed by Md Wais Hossain in obtaining entry in the record by practicing fraud. 

 20. It has further been stated that though the first inquiry committee failed to detect fraud but in subsequent inquiry fraud was detected, though the High Court Division has quoted only the first inquiry report but the High Court Division has over looked the second inquiry report given by Gokul Chandra Haider, Sadar Assistant Settlement Officer, wherein it has been clearly stated as under: 

 23. Since fraud was detected subsequently, Settlement Officer, has jurisdiction for issuing notice and making for hearing of the parties to decide the matter under Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. Thus, it is evident that the impugned Judgment and order passed by the High Court Division suffers from legal infirmity.
